reason: Both conversations wrongly treat this as a frost-free defrost-heater or thermostat fault, and neither asks about the plinth or housing ventilation or treats the cause as uncertain. Conversation 1 is cleaner and more efficient. It proposes a full defrost as the low-cost test, then sensibly moves to a letting-agent report once the tenant says they may report it. Conversation 2 spends turns on a drain-water check the tenant cannot do, and its replies are garbled with stray '1. 2. 3.' list fragments. It also ends by calling the symptoms 'classic' and naming the 'heater or thermostat' as the likely part, and it dismisses the defrost as only temporary. That is a more confident part claim with less support.
